message.content:
**What I did and why:** I researched Apple's most recent results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75, which filled at $222.75 (total ≈ $9,801 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, and the only order placed today, so well under the $20,000 daily cap; the limit was set essentially at the current market ask of $222.72, and no funds were moved out of the account).

**Key figures relied on:** Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) revenue of **$94.9B, up 6% year over year**; full fiscal 2024 net sales of **$391.0B** (vs. $383.3B in FY2023), net income of **$93.7B**, diluted EPS of **$6.08**, and operating income of **$123.2B** — with the caveat that FY2024 net income and EPS were depressed by a one-time **$10.2B** income tax charge, so underlying profitability was better than the headline decline suggests. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual rollout of Apple Intelligence, which leaves optionality around the holiday quarter without an obvious negative catalyst. Given solid top-line growth, a strong services/installed-base franchise, and a price near the middle of its recent range, I sized a modest starter position rather than a full allocation, keeping the rest of the mandate's capacity available for a potential MSFT or additional AAPL entry.
